prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using chemically induced proximity to recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases, and for identifying cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical mode of action: a designed heterobifunctional molecule or a glue reshapes a protein surface so that the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery removes a target, rather than a ligand simply occupying a site. The idea is original, was demonstrated in cells by the Crews and Deshaies PROTAC work, and has been reproduced across many laboratories, E3 ligases and target classes. The cereblon discovery by Handa and colleagues gives a mechanistic explanation for thalidomide, lenalidomide and pomalidomide that had been missing for decades, and ties the PROTAC and glue arms into one story of induced proximity. Opening ballots show broad convergence, with the candidate ranked first by three members and in the top four by all eight, which agrees with my own reading that it combines conceptual originality, molecular design and large downstream impact. From my own work on peptide-based receptors and biosensors, I also value that it is a case where chemical design of a binding interface translates into a therapeutic modality.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that no PROTAC has yet been approved as a drug, so the clinical vindication that usually accompanies a prize of this kind is still pending, and the committee could reasonably prefer to wait. The second is attribution: a three-person cap forces us to choose among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and any choice leaves out people with decisive contributions, notably Ciulli on VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure, and Ito on cereblon. Pairing the PROTAC concept with the cereblon and glue discovery in one citation may also read as two achievements stitched together.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for B057, argues that Ciulli supplied the VHL-based structural and chemical foundation and the ternary-complex mechanism, and says credit for molecular glues is separate and may need a different configuration.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli argument seriously, and the VHL ligand work was what made PROTACs drug-like and mechanistically understood. But I would still place Handa ahead of Ciulli, because cereblon underlies the largest clinical class of degraders and answers the thalidomide puzzle, which gives the prize a mechanistic core as well as a design concept. I agree with the concern that PROTAC and glue credit are distinct lineages; my reply is that a single citation on chemically induced proximity covers both without needing a second part. If the committee wants to honour Ciulli I would want to know who is displaced, and I do not see a clean answer yet.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Buchwald and Hartwig's Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first, as a general, durable method with decades of industrial use, an obvious two-person configuration and a topic that the 2010 cross-coupling prize did not cover.
responses.response: I accept that B068 is the cleanest case on attribution and maturity on the list, and I do not dispute its quality. My reservation is that it is a refinement within a methodology class already honoured in 2010, so its conceptual novelty relative to the earlier prize is smaller than that of a new mode of action. I would put it as the safest option rather than the most original, and I would be comfortable seeing it recognised later or alongside another prize part if the committee wants a two-part configuration. I do not want maturity to be read as superiority.

responses.point: Chabes places B057 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that PROTACs and the cereblon mechanism together span concept and mechanism, and that the ubiquitin-proteasome biochemistry is well established, while noting that no degrader is approved yet.
responses.response: I agree with the configuration and with Chabes's reasoning that these three best span concept and mechanism. I would add that the maturity worry is partly answered by the biochemistry: ternary-complex formation and degradation kinetics are well characterised and independently confirmed, so the question is clinical rather than scientific. Where I would go further than Chabes is on the cost of the cap, since Gray and Ciulli built much of the chemical toolbox, and I would want the citation worded so that it does not imply they were overlooked on scientific grounds.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates (B005) first as a physical-chemical reframing of cellular organisation, and ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B064) second as applied lipid self-assembly, placing B057 fourth.
responses.response: I agree that condensates are conceptually major, and my own self-assembly and peptide interests make me sympathetic. My hesitation is whether the headline discovery is chemistry or cell biology, and whether the field has settled how widely function depends on true phase separation, which Sparr herself notes. B057 has a sharper, testable chemical claim and a clearer set of laureates. On B064, I see the societal impact but the credit is crowded and the 2023 Medicine prize overlaps. I would keep B005 as a strong alternative rather than my first choice.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello dynamics (B037) first as an overdue computational chemistry foundation with a clean two-person attribution, and ranks B057 fourth because no PROTAC drug is approved and attribution is complex.
responses.response: The Car-Parrinello case is clean and I do not question its importance. I disagree with the timing argument against B057: independent confirmation of the mechanism is strong, and previous prizes have recognised enabling chemical concepts before the whole clinical story was finished. I do share his concern about attribution complexity, and I would accept that if the committee cannot agree a three-person split for B057, B037 is a better-defined option than forcing a contested one.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the absence of an approved PROTAC drug as disqualifying or acceptable given the mechanistic and clinical-trial evidence.
How to allocate credit between the PROTAC lineage (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto) and the cereblon and molecular-glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Gray, Kim) within three names.
Whether a single citation on induced proximity is cleaner than splitting the prize into two parts.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I note a field closeness to peptide, protein and biosensing chemistry (B054, B010-type work, plasmonics), and a research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly, which bears on B005 and B064; none is a personal or institutional tie to a named candidate.
